module.purpose: Provides server-side authorization rules for comment, comment-thread, and comment-reaction records in a synchronized collaboration room.
module.summary: This module builds record authorizers that gate all comment writes through session access, enforce session-derived attribution, protect immutable structural fields, and distinguish soft deletion from ordinary edits. It supports configurable commenting and per-write authorization while preserving canonical reaction identifiers, thread resolution attribution, write-once deletion flags, and server-only hard deletion semantics.
module.businessContext: Supports collaborative document comments and reactions with trustworthy authorship and moderation controls. If authorization fails, users may forge attribution, alter comment relationships, or perform unauthorized deletion.
functions: createCommentAuthorizers (~L121-330): Builds authorization rules for all supported comment record types.
withUserId (~L141-149): Gates writes and resolves the session user identity once.
authorizeAuthored (~L155-172): Stamps attribution and enforces immutable ownership fields.
authorizeSoftDeleted (~L185-214): Enforces soft-delete lifecycle and modification permissions.
immutableFields (~L241-254): Rejects updates that alter protected record fields.

typeShapes.name: CommentModification
CommentModificationAuthContext
CommentAuthorizerOptions
typeShapes.shape:
{
	/**
	 * Resolve the authenticated user id for a session from its host-provided `meta`. Return `null`
	 * for anonymous sessions — they can't create records, and own none, so the default
	 * {@link CommentAuthorizerOptions.canModifyComment} grants them no edits or deletes either.
	 */
	getUserId(session: { sessionId: string; isReadonly: boolean; meta: SessionMeta }): string | null

	/**
	 * Whether a session may write comment records at all — checked before the per-type rules.
	 * Defaults to `({ isReadonly }) => !isReadonly`, so read-only viewers can read threads but not
	 * post. Override to decouple the lanes: `() => true` allows commenting on a read-only canvas.
	 */
	canComment?(session: { sessionId: string; isReadonly: boolean; meta: SessionMeta }): boolean

	/**
	 * Whether a session may make a particular write against a particular stored record: editing or
	 * deleting a comment, or deleting a thread. Defaults to `({ userId, ownerId }) => userId === ownerId` — the owner-only rule enforced up to now.
	 * Override to widen it (a workspace admin or moderator who may take down anyone's comment) or
	 * to narrow it (no edits after an hour).
	 *
	 * The counterpart to `canModifyComment` in `@tldraw/commenting`, which decides which
	 * affordances the UI offers. This one is the real rule, and the two want widening together: a
	 * delete the client offers and this rejects is applied locally, vetoed, and rebased away — the
	 * comment comes back with nothing to explain it.
	 *
	 * Asked after {@link CommentAuthorizerOptions.canComment} and after the structural rules, so it
	 * can only widen *who* may write, never *what* a write may contain. However permissive the
	 * callback, attribution is still stamped from the session and immutable, `isDeleted` is still
	 * write-once and never set at create, `threadId` and `createdAt` are still frozen, a
	 * resolution is still the resolver's own, and clients still can't hard-delete.
	 *
	 * A soft delete that changes anything besides the flag is asked about twice — once as the
	 * delete, once as an edit — so granting deletes alone can't be talked into an edit.
	 *
	 * Called at most once per authorized write, twice for that combined case.
	 *
	 * @example
	 * ```ts
	 * createCommentAuthorizers<SessionMeta>({
	 * 	getUserId: (session) => session.meta.userId,
	 * 	// Moderators may take anything down. Editing stays the author's, whoever you are.
	 * 	canModifyComment: (ctx) =>
	 * 		(ctx.action !== 'edit-comment' && isModerator(ctx.session.meta)) ||
	 * 		ctx.userId === ctx.ownerId,
	 * })
	 * ```
	 */
	canModifyComment?(ctx: CommentModificationAuthContext<SessionMeta>): boolean
}

moduleContractTests.scenario: An anonymous session attempts to create a comment, thread, or reaction.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Records requiring attribution must not be created without an authenticated user.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An authenticated session creates an authored comment or reaction.
moduleContractTests.then: the returned record has authorId or userId equal to 'user-1'
moduleContractTests.rationale: Attribution is always taken from the session rather than client input.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A read-only session attempts any comment record write using the default access gate.
moduleContractTests.rationale: The default canComment policy denies writes from read-only viewers.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An update changes a comment author, reaction user, or thread creator.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Authorship fields cannot be forged or transferred after creation.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An update changes a comment threadId or createdAt, or a reaction identity field.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Structural identity and ordering fields are frozen after creation.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A client attempts to remove a comment or thread record directly.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Client deletion is represented only by a soft-delete flag.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A client creates a comment or thread with isDeleted already set.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Deletion is write-once and cannot be smuggled into record creation.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An update attempts to clear an existing soft-delete flag.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Soft deletion is irreversible until server-side pruning.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A soft-delete update also changes another field and the caller has delete permission but not edit permission.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Delete permission must not authorize unrelated edits bundled into the same write.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An authenticated user resolves or reopens a thread with their own user id in the resolution attribution.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Resolution is open to room members but its attribution must belong to the acting user.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A thread update assigns a non-null resolution to another user's identity.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Clients cannot claim that another user resolved the thread.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A user creates a reaction whose id does not match its comment, user, and emoji tuple.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Canonical ids prevent reaction-slot squatting and duplicate triples.

import type { UnknownRecord } from '@tldraw/store'
import type { TLRecordAuthorizer, TLRecordAuthorizers } from '@tldraw/sync-core'
import {
	createCommentReactionId,
	type TLComment,
	type TLCommentReaction,
	type TLCommentThread,
} from '@tldraw/tlschema'
import { isEqual } from '@tldraw/utils'

units.name: createCommentAuthorizers

detail.name: createCommentAuthorizers
preconditions: opts is provided and supplies a getUserId callback.
The returned authorizers are invoked with sessions and record-operation arguments matching TLRecordAuthorizer contracts.
postconditions: Returns a TLRecordAuthorizers map covering TLComment, TLCommentThread, and TLCommentReaction records.
Each authorization operation first applies canComment, defaulting to rejection for readonly sessions.
Each authorized operation resolves the session user id once before applying record-specific rules.
Default policies permit commenting only when isReadonly is false and permit comment modification only when userId equals ownerId.
invariants: Attribution fields stamped during creation are derived from the resolved session user id rather than trusted client attribution.
Attribution and structural identity fields remain immutable on updates where the record-specific rules require them.
Soft-deleted records cannot be created as already deleted, undeleted, or hard-deleted through client authorization.
Reaction identity remains tied to commentId, the resolved user id, and emoji.
edgeCases: If canComment returns false, the operation is rejected without applying the record-specific rule.
If a create operation has no resolved user id, authored records are rejected.
If no canComment callback is supplied, readonly sessions are rejected and non-readonly sessions are allowed through the gate.
If no canModifyComment callback is supplied, modifications are allowed only when the resolved user id equals the record owner.
A client delete of a reaction is accepted only when the resolved user id matches the reaction's userId; server-initiated pruning is outside these client authorizers.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Rejects unauthorized or structurally invalid operations by returning null from the applicable authorizer; it does not define a thrown-error contract.
errorPolicy.returnsOnError: The applicable record authorizer returns null.

detail.summary: Creates record authorizers for comments, comment threads, and comment reactions. The authorizers derive identity from session metadata, gate writes by comment access policy, and enforce attribution and record-specific mutation rules.

specTests.then: It returns null and does not authorize the operation.

detail.name: authorizeAuthored
preconditions: The record attribution field is configured by the enclosing authorizer factory.
A session capable of resolving a user id is supplied when authorization is evaluated.
postconditions: A newly authorized record has its attribution field stamped with the session user id.
An authorized update cannot alter the attribution field.
When owner-only updates are enabled, only the record author may update the record.
invariants: Record attribution is immutable after creation.
The attribution value is derived from the authenticated session rather than trusted create input.
edgeCases: Create operations overwrite or stamp the attribution field with the session user id.
Updates attempting to change the attribution field are rejected.
When owner-only update behavior is enabled, updates by a non-author are rejected even if they do not change attribution.
Sessions that fail the enclosing comment authorization gate are rejected.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Returns null for unauthorized operations, including attempts to violate attribution immutability or owner-only update restrictions.

detail.summary: Creates an authorizer for records whose attribution is stored in a designated field. On creation, the field is stamped from the session user; on update, the attribution remains immutable, with optional restriction of all updates to the author.

units.name: authorizeSoftDeleted

detail.name: authorizeSoftDeleted
detail.signature: function authorizeSoftDeleted<Rec extends UnknownRecord & { isDeleted: boolean }>(ownerOf: (rec: Rec) => string, modificationFor: (rec: Rec, write: 'edit' | 'delete') => CommentModification | null, base: Rule<Rec>): Rule<Rec>
preconditions: ownerOf identifies the author of a record.
modificationFor returns the applicable comment modification authorization or null for a given record and write kind.
base is a valid authorization rule for Rec.
Records contain a boolean isDeleted field.
postconditions: A client delete operation is rejected.
A create operation cannot create a record with isDeleted set.
An update that changes isDeleted is classified as a delete write; other updates are classified as edit writes.
An update combining a deletion-state change with other edits must satisfy both the delete and edit authorization requirements.
Authorization denied by base or by the applicable modification authorization returns null.
invariants: The isDeleted field is write-once from false to true and cannot be unset.
Hard deletion is server-initiated rather than client-authorized.
A modificationFor result of null means that authorization is not requested for that write and base remains the governing rule.
Authorization for a deletion-state change is distinct from authorization for ordinary edits.
edgeCases: A delete-typed request returns null without delegating to base.
A create request attempting to set isDeleted is rejected.
An update that only changes isDeleted is treated as a delete rather than an edit.
An update that changes both isDeleted and other fields must pass both relevant authorization checks.
An update that does not change isDeleted is treated as an edit; resolve or reopen-style changes can therefore be governed by base when modificationFor does not request a separate authorization.
An already soft-deleted record cannot be undeleted.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Returns null for unauthorized, hard-delete, create-with-isDeleted, undelete, or otherwise invalid writes.

detail.summary: Returns a rule that applies base authorization to soft-deleted comment records while separately authorizing edits and deletion-state changes. It prevents client hard-deletes, creation of already-deleted records, and unauthorized or combined writes that bypass either authorization gate.

specLiterals.role: Identifies an ordinary record modification for modificationFor.
Identifies a change to the soft-deletion state for modificationFor.
The contractual record field controlling soft deletion.

specTests.when: The returned authorization rule is invoked.
specTests.then: It returns null and does not authorize the client hard-delete.

specTests.when: The returned authorization rule is invoked.
The returned authorization rule is invoked.
specTests.then: The write is treated as both a delete and an edit, and authorization succeeds only if both gates permit it.

units.name: immutableFields

detail.name: immutableFields
preconditions: The authorization arguments identify a create or update operation and provide the corresponding comment-thread records.
postconditions: Returns null when authored access is denied.
For create operations, rejects a resolved value whose by field differs from the caller user ID.
For update operations, rejects changes to resolved.at or resolved.by when the resulting resolved.by differs from the caller user ID.
invariants: A resolution author introduced or changed by this authorization rule must equal the calling user ID.
Existing resolution fields are accepted when they are unchanged during an update.
edgeCases: If authorizeAuthored for createdBy returns a falsy result, authorization returns null without applying resolution-specific checks.
On create, a truthy resolved value authored by another user is rejected with null.
On update, changes to resolved.at or resolved.by are rejected when next.resolved exists and its by field belongs to another user.
On update, unchanged resolution fields do not trigger the resolution-author check.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Returns null when authored authorization fails or when a newly assigned or changed resolution is attributed to another user.

detail.summary: Authorizes comment-thread resolution changes only when the caller is authorized as the creator and any newly assigned resolution author matches the caller.

specTests.then: The resolution-specific checks do not reject the operation.
